@0170B 'ne Judaei, qui excusationem ignorantiae non habent, non occidant' — zoomed on BOTH copies. Both non present on both. Migne's, and the ground of this stint's one [cj:].

@0172A PRESS VARIANT, both copies clean, neither at fault: Gallica prints 'rerurrectionis' (split re- / rurrectionis) and the archive prints 'resurrectionis'. Our TEI follows Gallica. No [sic:] (it would need two witnesses and the second refutes it), no patch (the twin reproduces its own copy faithfully). Crux only. The first site in this range where the archive copy is the cleaner of the two.
@0172C archive prints 'ut inde caetera contexereunt'; Gallica prints 'contexerent'. Archive ink, and a non-word. Our TEI right.

@0175A the Wisdom quotation ('de manu contrariorum', 'respectus in sermonibus illius', 'Si enim vere Filius Dei est') read letter by letter on both; identical on both. [var:] fired against Sap 2:20 and 2:18.

The archive copy's running head on this page prints 'THOLOGICA' for THEOLOGICA; Gallica f88 prints it correctly. Running heads are not part of our TEI; recorded only as a further measurement of that copy's condition.

reads.footContents: THE WORK'S LAST PAGE, re-read on BOTH copies at full resolution as the launch message required. Matthew closes at 'Sic veniet quemadmodum vidistis eum euntem in coelum (Act. I).' in col 0178D; a short centred rule stands below it; the remaining ~two-fifths of the leaf is blank paper. NO note, NO asterisk, NO colophon, on EITHER copy. The single-witness 150 dpi spot check is hereby confirmed by a second witness at 300 dpi.
findings: @0177A archive prints 'VERS. 66. — Munierum sepulcrum'; Gallica prints 'Munierunt'. Archive ink, and a non-word. Our TEI right.
@0178A both plates print the note as '(Joan. XX)' with a period after Joan; our TEI prints '(Joan XX)'. OUR defect, minor. Pending TEI patch.

@0178D archive prints 'Et ecce ego vobiscum suum'; Gallica prints 'sum'. Archive ink. Our TEI right — and this is the work's closing lemma, so a false claim here would have stood at the most conspicuous point in the book.
The two abridgment-formula 'usque ad' spans (@0177B and @0178D) are italic on both copies and both follow an 'etc.', as our TEI has them.

methodNotes: Both maps were computed from the columns wanted and then checked against the printed corner numbers before anything on the page was read.

Nineteen candidates raised on the archive copy; nineteen refuted at Gallica; none confirmed. Nine of the nineteen were non-words, which under the CORRECTION TO ADDENDUM A is a reason to fetch the second witness and not a substitute for it — it was right nine times out of nine here.
Two disagreements between the copies are press variants with both copies clean (@0172A rerurrectionis/resurrectionis, @0172D the VERS. 4 dash). Neither is a defect to accuse anyone of; crux only.
Feet of all six pages inspected on both copies. Checked zero: no apparatus of any kind in cols 0167-0178.
